boundary_condition: If inventory is at risk, only hold cancellable rooms or fare holds while waiting for the missing details.
default_action: Draft a non-booking plan, ask the client for the missing operational details, then route one approval-ready package with open items called out.

evidence.quote: Let’s not book until I get the address and Friday timing. What should I ask the client?
Okay. Don’t book anything yet. Just give me the skeleton I can paste into my notes.
I don’t want to overbuild this before the client confirms. What should I ask them?
Great. Give me a tentative plan I can share internally, but mark it as not ready to book.
For approval I need a shortlist, not final booking. Keep the hotel well-rated—around 4.0 or better from guests if possible. Breakfast is helpful but not the deciding factor.

exception_condition: Proceed to booking once manager approval is in and the unresolved items no longer affect the flight, hotel area, or transport choice.
name: Hold work bookings until site and agenda details are firm
preference_value: Work trips should stay provisional until the exact client or organizer site, first required onsite time, return-day end time, and local transport assumptions are known.
scope_condition: Solo work/client/conference trips where the address, Monday requirement, Thursday wrap, or transport plan is still uncertain.

boundary_condition: Do not pay a large premium or accept a worse day just to fly Delta.
default_action: Include Delta in the comparison and select it when the schedule and total price are comparable.

evidence.quote: From ATL, Delta is nice if comparable, but I’m fine with another carrier.
Use Delta if the 5:40-ish outbound and Tuesday afternoon return are still close to American.
Can you include Delta if it’s close, but don’t force it if another nonstop is much cheaper?
That sounds right. Delta is fine if the schedule is sensible, but I don’t need to force it. No long layovers for this.
For MSP I would prefer a nonstop if the timing is decent. Delta is fine if it is not absurd.
For now, assume ATL to MSP, economy, Monday to Thursday. If a Delta nonstop is close on price, include it, but don't force it.

exception_condition: Choose another carrier when it is meaningfully cheaper, has better times, or better family seat availability.
name: Use Delta as a tie-breaker, not a mandate
preference_value: Delta is preferred when price and timing are close, but carrier preference should not override a materially better schedule or fare on another airline.
scope_condition: Atlanta-origin itineraries where Delta and another nonstop carrier are both available.

boundary_condition: Main Cabin does not need to be fully refundable; the key is seat selection and usable change rules.
default_action: Book Main Cabin/economy standard fares and do not prepay extras unless needed.

evidence.quote: Okay. Main Cabin, not Basic. For seats, three together if possible, but if not, one adult next to our child matters more than all three being in the same row.
Go ahead with those. Main Cabin, not Basic.
What about fare type? I don’t want to accidentally lose the seat assignments.

Correct. Main Cabin, carry-on only, work card. Please get a window seat even if it’s behind the wing.

exception_condition: Basic Economy is not used in recurring examples where seating or flexibility matters; consider only if seat placement is irrelevant and savings are compelling.
name: Avoid Basic Economy when seat control or flexibility matters
preference_value: Use Main Cabin or equivalent standard economy rather than Basic Economy when advance seat selection, family seating, or work-trip change flexibility matters.
scope_condition: Family trips and work trips where assigned seats, changes, or schedule stability are important.

boundary_condition: Avoid last-row or poor seats when possible, and do not pay preferred-seat fees just to move a few rows.
default_action: Select adjacent seats first; take a window within that arrangement when available; for solo flights choose a no-fee window over a forward aisle or middle.

evidence.quote: For seats, three together if possible, but if not, one adult next to our child matters more than all three being in the same row.
Seats matter more with the kid. Can you keep us together, and if there’s a window for me, use it?
Put Nia by the window outbound. For the return I’ll take the window unless she insists. Main thing is not splitting us up.
Seats next. I want our child between us or right next to both of us. If I can get the window, great, but together matters more.
Seat maps show a few windows toward the back. Forward seats are mostly aisle or middle. I’d rather take a window than a forward aisle, as long as it is not the last row.
Take the rear windows. A forward middle is not worth it. Also add a quiet-room request at the hotel if there is a field for it.

exception_condition: If a full family row is unavailable, use a child-plus-adult pair with the other adult across the aisle or nearby.
name: Seat selection prioritizes togetherness, then no-fee windows
preference_value: For family trips, keep the group together and ensure the child is next to an adult; for solo/work flights, take a no-fee window even if farther back, but do not pay or split the group just for seat location.
scope_condition: Seat assignment on booked flights for both family and solo work travel.

boundary_condition: Anything below roughly 4.0 needs a clearly stated reason and tradeoff.
default_action: Filter to well-reviewed properties first, then compare location, breakfast, dinner, room setup, and cancellation terms.

Please don't include anything with weak reviews. Four stars or better if possible.
And please don’t send me anything with weak reviews just because it’s cheaper.

exception_condition: If the destination has very limited options, flag the quality issue rather than hiding it in a cheap recommendation.
name: Use a strong guest-review floor for hotels
preference_value: Hotels should generally have solid guest reviews around 4.0+; do not accept weak, sketchy, noisy, or poorly reviewed lodging just to save money.
scope_condition: Hotel shortlists for work and family trips.

boundary_condition: A less convenient dinner situation is acceptable only when the location or room setup clearly wins and rideshares are easy.
default_action: Prefer hotels near restaurants or with an on-site restaurant/bar, even if breakfast is paid or room rate is slightly higher.

I want simple flights into Tampa or Sarasota, a Sunday return that doesn't wreck Monday, and a hotel or condo setup where beach, pool, breakfast or groceries, and casual dinners are easy with a kid.
I will not have a car, so dinner nearby matters if we land late or I am done late.
Please include breakfast and dinner access when you compare later, but I agree area is first.

exception_condition: For beach or family stays, groceries/cafes can solve breakfast, but casual dinner nearby remains important.
name: Require easy dinner access at hotels
preference_value: Hotels should have on-site dining or easy nearby casual dinner options so evenings after work, flights, or family activities are not a production.
scope_condition: Hotel selection for no-car work trips, family weekends, beach stays, and late-arrival days.

boundary_condition: A slightly higher refundable rate is acceptable for flexibility.
default_action: Book or hold cancellable rates, verify cancellation cutoff, and keep backup options only until the preferred reservation is safe.

exception_condition: A prepaid rate may be considered only when trip risk is low and the savings are meaningful, but recent behavior favors cancellable options even at a higher rate.
name: Prefer cancellable hotel bookings and avoid prepaid rates while plans can change
preference_value: Hotel bookings should usually be refundable/cancellable, with cancellation deadlines tracked; prepaid or nonrefundable rates are avoided unless plans are very firm and savings justify the risk.
scope_condition: Work and family hotel reservations, especially before schedules, PTO, client agendas, or weather-sensitive plans are fully stable.

boundary_condition: Treat these as requests, not guarantees; do not change otherwise good hotels solely because the request cannot be guaranteed.
default_action: Add quiet-room and away-from-elevator requests at booking, and repeat or confirm them at check-in when relevant.

Please also add a quiet-room request for the hotel, away from elevators if possible.

exception_condition: High-floor requests can be omitted when the important part is simply avoiding elevator/noise exposure.
name: Add quiet-room hotel requests by default
preference_value: Ask hotels for a quiet room, usually away from elevators, ice machines, and street/noise sources; high floor is often preferred when available.
scope_condition: Hotel bookings for work and family trips where notes or special requests can be added.

boundary_condition: A remote airport becomes viable when it saves several hundred dollars total and does not create a late or complicated arrival.

exception_condition: If the convenient airport fare spikes sharply or seats/schedule are poor, recompare remote airport plus ground transfer before booking.
name: For short family city trips, pay a reasonable premium for easier city access

boundary_condition: Two doubles can be tolerated for a short two-night stay if ratings, location, breakfast, and cancellation are strong.
default_action: Book a family-suitable room type, verify bed setup, and favor larger rooms for longer stays.

exception_condition: Do not accept one bed plus uncertain rollaway/sofa arrangements unless the hotel confirms the setup.
name: Family hotel rooms must genuinely work for three
preference_value: For family stays, room setup and breathing room matter: two queens are preferred; a king plus a real sofa bed can work; tiny or uncertain rooms are avoided even if breakfast is included.
scope_condition: Family hotel selection for city, museum, and long-weekend trips with two adults and a child.

boundary_condition: If the obligation is optional, remote, explicitly flexible, or the current itinerary still has a real cushion, the user will consider the leaner or cheaper option.
default_action: Choose the earlier nonstop, previous-day arrival, later return, or extra hotel night when needed to avoid sprinting or risking the first/last obligation.

Let’s not do the Thursday sprint. Book the Friday morning return.

exception_condition: The user may accept a tighter plan only after consciously accepting the risk and keeping baggage/ground logistics lean; comfort alone is not enough to add nights.
name: Protect fixed-event buffers over convenience and small savings
preference_value: For schedule-sensitive trainings, certifications, client setup windows, equipment handoffs, and debriefs, the user prefers itinerary buffer over a cheaper fare, a later departure, or avoiding an extra hotel night.
scope_condition: Work or certification travel with fixed start times, setup/calibration/handoff windows, checked equipment, or uncertain end times.

boundary_condition: A one-stop itinerary is acceptable when nonstop fares are unreasonable, no nonstop exists, or the fare difference is meaningfully large.
default_action: Start with nonstop options; if connecting, use one comfortable layover and avoid tight or long connections, especially with holidays, weather, or equipment.

I’m okay with a connection, just not a two-stop mess or a layover that eats half the day.

I don’t want a two-hour airport sit just to save $90.

exception_condition: Do not pick a worse connection merely for a preferred airline or small savings.
name: Prefer nonstops and simple routing over carrier loyalty
preference_value: The user prefers nonstop flights or simple one-stop itineraries, with schedule reliability more important than airline loyalty. One reasonable layover is acceptable when needed or when savings are large; two stops, long sits, and brittle connections are disfavored.
scope_condition: Flights from Denver for work, family, and leisure trips.

boundary_condition: The user does not require premium cabins; price sensitivity remains within regular economy.
default_action: Book regular economy/main cabin rather than basic economy, then select seats during or soon after booking.

exception_condition: On low-cost carriers, the user may buy carry-on and seat selection à la carte if the total remains worthwhile.
name: Book regular economy/main cabin, not basic economy
preference_value: Coach/economy is fine, but the user wants normal seat selection, carry-on rights, and standard flexibility; basic economy is normally avoided.
scope_condition: Air ticketing for solo work travel and couple/family trips where seat choice and carry-on access matter.

For seats, same as Indy: window if it is not the last row, aisle over a last-row window, and no middle.

exception_condition: If the only window is poor, take an aisle over a last-row window or middle seat; avoid exit rows unless explicitly acceptable.
name: Window-seat preference with practical limits
preference_value: The user prefers a decent window seat, but avoids exit rows, last-row/no-recline compromises, and middle seats. When traveling with a spouse/companion, sitting together outranks getting the perfect window.
scope_condition: Flight seat selection for both solo and companion travel.

boundary_condition: Commute, parking, review quality, and schedule reliability can override the hot tub or pool.
default_action: Prefer hotels that have fitness access and, when feasible, pool/hot tub amenities; confirm amenity hours when they matter.

For hotels I care about good reviews and a real gym; pool or hot tub would be a plus for the weekend.
For hotels, I’d like 4.0 or better if possible, and pool/hot tub/gym would be useful after training days.

I use a gym or pool if it is there, and a hot tub is nice, but not worth a silly commute.

preference_value: A usable fitness room or real gym is a recurring priority; pool access is useful, and a hot tub/soaking option is valued for recovery but is normally a bonus rather than the deciding factor.
scope_condition: Hotel selection across work trips and leisure stays, especially after standing-heavy training days or hiking weekends.

boundary_condition: A farther hotel can win only if the work commute remains reasonable or if a confirmed spouse/weekend extension changes the purpose of the stay.

preference_value: On work trips, the user prefers a hotel close to the actual site or central to the clinic loop, with easy parking/unloading, over a downtown location, better restaurant scene, or hot tub.
scope_condition: Client training, rollout, calibration, and multi-site work trips, especially with demo cases or workbooks.

boundary_condition: Multiple holds are acceptable only if cancellation deadlines are clear and the user will not forget to release extras.

exception_condition: Do not pay for a guaranteed view/balcony if it makes the rate nonrefundable unless explicitly reapproved.
name: Prefer cancellable/refundable lodging and avoid prepaid locks while plans are uncertain
preference_value: The user strongly prefers cancellable/refundable hotel rates and avoids prepaid/nonrefundable bookings when schedules, spouse participation, or site locations are uncertain.
scope_condition: Hotel reservations, split stays, backup holds, and leisure rooms with uncertain timing or amenities.

boundary_condition: A standard SUV is acceptable when spouse gear or additional cartons justify it; a compact/midsize car is fine only for light personal trips.

Standard SUV, with midsize SUV as fallback. No sedan unless there’s no choice and you ask me.

name: Choose SUV/crossover class for gear, not sedan; avoid oversizing unless needed
preference_value: When transporting demo/analyzer cases, cartons, or family gear, the user prefers a compact/midsize/standard SUV or crossover with easy loading rather than a sedan; she also avoids unnecessarily oversized vehicles.
scope_condition: Rental car class selection for clinic rollouts, equipment travel, and family trips with extra cargo.

boundary_condition: Alternate airports or cheaper routings remain candidates only when net savings are substantial and the drive/weather/timing is acceptable.

Milwaukee if at all possible. I do not want to add O’Hare and a rental drive to a holiday week unless the savings are ridiculous.

exception_condition: If savings become truly large or budget is the controlling factor, the user will reconsider the less convenient option.
name: Evaluate total trip cost and hassle, not just headline fare
preference_value: The user compares door-to-door package cost and hassle, including rental cars, hotels, parking, tolls, pickups, and late arrivals. Small savings are not worth added driving, alternate airports, hotels, or misconnect risk.
scope_condition: Choosing between airports, flight times, connections, late arrivals, and hotel/car packages for work, family, and leisure trips.

boundary_condition: Fixed pieces such as a definite destination flight or cancellable hotel may be held earlier if fares/rooms are at risk.
default_action: Ask the coordinator/client targeted questions and use conditional branches or cancellable holds until the key logistics are confirmed.

scope_condition: Client trainings, analyzer rollouts, certification labs, and multi-site clinic trips with uncertain schedules or equipment.

preference_value: The user prefers carry-on-only personal travel when feasible, especially for conferences and tight arrivals. Checked baggage is acceptable for demo/training cases or consumables, but critical items should remain in the carry-on/personal item.
scope_condition: Packing and baggage decisions for flights, especially with certification check-ins, weather, or equipment risk.

boundary_condition: The user will not pay nonrefundable or excessive premiums merely for a view/balcony, and family-event logistics or budget can shift the hotel choice more practical.
default_action: Hold/request cancellable resort, oceanfront, lodge, or recovery-style rooms; plan reasonable arrival/return times and avoid over-scheduled or driving-heavy weekends.

boundary_condition: Do not pay a large premium or accept weaker timing just to fly United.

boundary_condition: A one-stop itinerary must save meaningfully more than a small fare gap and must not create a tight arrival, tight return, or late homecoming.

exception_condition: Use a scheduled/local SUV or XL rideshare instead of a rental when the main problem is a one-time gear drop and parking would be more annoying than useful.

preference_value: Do not rent by default; use rideshare or scheduled SUV when it avoids parking friction, but rent a compact/pay-later car when gear, early starts, suburban sites, groceries, or confirmed parking make control more valuable.
scope_condition: Local transport decisions for work trips, conferences, clinic trainings, and car-based leisure weekends.

boundary_condition: Ask for extra specifics when materials are bulky, temperature-sensitive, or need overnight security.
default_action: Send a concise question list to the host or conference office and let the answers determine flights, hotel, rental, and return timing.

exception_condition: Once access, storage, and timing are confirmed, proceed with the practical travel stack; if answers remain vague, choose safer transport/hotel/return buffers or do not book.
name: Gate work-trip bookings on host logistics for access, storage, equipment, and entrances
preference_value: Before committing to clinic or conference travel, require concrete host answers on room access, entry points, parking/loading, storage, equipment/AV, teardown or release time, and contact procedures.
scope_condition: Work trips involving teaching, demo gear, lab materials, conference presentations, or hospital/clinic buildings.

boundary_condition: If flight, drive, rental pickup, badge, or setup timing slips, skip groceries and use delivery, hotel market, or next-day shopping.

name: Keep arrival food and groceries simple and conditional
preference_value: Do not improvise late meals or squeeze in groceries when timing is tight; plan simple food around the room fridge/coffee, packed snacks, delivery, or a brief grocery stop only if travel is on time.
scope_condition: Trips with late arrivals, early clinic starts, first-night setup, road trips, or partner recovery weekends.

Start with SFO. OAK or SJC only if they clearly beat it.

preference_value: SFO is the default Bay Area airport. Oakland is acceptable only when it is materially cleaner, cheaper, or operationally better. San Jose is usually excluded unless it is an obvious win.

boundary_condition: Once the user says to book/proceed and the blocking items are settled, complete the booking using the chosen plan.
default_action: Prepare ranked recommendations and keep open items visible; ask before booking flights, hotels, cars, or extra nights.

scope_condition: Any trip that includes pending client approval, freight/gear delivery, site timing, meeting uncertainty, hotel deadline, or personal schedule uncertainty.

boundary_condition: A lower-rated hotel is only considered if there is a specific operational reason and no decent alternative.
default_action: Screen out mediocre properties; rank hotels with strong guest feedback and practical fit over the cheapest or closest option.

preference_value: Hotels should be solidly reviewed, generally 4.0+ when practical, and not marginal, tired, or bare-bones just because they are cheap, close, or official.
scope_condition: Work hotels, conference hotels, and leisure hotels where there are viable alternatives.

boundary_condition: Do not overpay solely for coffee/fridge if a better overall hotel is available; for leisure weekends, room basics may be less important than walkability or vibe.
default_action: Check room details for in-room coffee maker, mini-fridge, and desk/workspace; add notes requesting/confirming them, plus quiet-room notes when relevant.

exception_condition: If amenities are request-only, flag them for check-in and keep an acceptable backup if the amenity is mission-critical for samples or early departures.
name: Verify practical in-room work amenities, especially coffee and mini-fridge
preference_value: For work stays, the room should be functional: in-room coffee and mini-fridge are repeatedly requested, with desk/workspace important when slide review is expected. These should be confirmed or added as reservation notes, not assumed from lobby amenities.
scope_condition: Business hotels, early-start plant trips, conference hotels, and stays involving samples, slides, or long workdays.

boundary_condition: If no free window is available, choose an aisle or leave the seat for later rather than paying solely for a window.
default_action: Select no-fee window seats for solo trips; avoid paid seat upgrades and exit-row assumptions unless asked; for two-person trips, select adjacent seats first.

No checked bags. Put us together even if that means no window.

Seats together first; window only if it doesn't split us.

exception_condition: Open-seating carriers require check-in reminders or EarlyBird only when explicitly approved; do not add paid early boarding by default.
name: Seat policy: free window when solo; adjacent seats when traveling with wife
preference_value: When traveling solo, choose a free window seat when available, with no paid seat upgrades. When traveling with his wife, sitting together is more important than window/aisle preference.
scope_condition: Flight bookings with selectable seats, including business and personal travel.

boundary_condition: Do not use off-airport rental agencies when terminal pickup protects timing; do not rent a car for downtown convention trips unless a site visit is added.

exception_condition: For personal city/weekend trips, skip the rental when the hotel and dinners are walkable, unless a hike/day trip requires one.
name: Use rental cars for plant access; size up to compact SUV when gear, roads, or weather justify it
preference_value: For site and plant trips, rent at the airport and avoid relying on rideshare at plant gates. Compact is fine for simple trips, but compact SUV is preferred when carrying gear, using muddy/gravel roads, or dealing with weather. For urban conferences, no rental unless there is an offsite visit.

boundary_condition: A short walk is acceptable when guest feedback, quiet-room odds, breakfast, or dinner access improve enough; avoid hotel switches mid-event unless necessary.

boundary_condition: A rental car is acceptable for airport transfer or a specific hike/day trip, but not just to reach dinner. A convenience premium is acceptable when it keeps a two- or three-night trip easy.

boundary_condition: Small packages can go to a hotel if confirmed, but heavy/critical cases should go to the distributor/plant/decorator when possible.
